name: wolfbook
description: Mathematica-style Wolfram Language notebooks in VS Code. Open existing .nb files, run a live Wolfram kernel, render LaTeX/graphics, debug code, and let Copilot, Claude Code or MCP agents evaluate cells.

cellUri.description: URI of the notebook cell to debug (auto-filled)

enumDescriptions: Auto-detect: changed cells use Refine mode, unchanged cells use Advance mode
Always advance: scroll to output and move focus to next cell after every evaluation
Always refine: no scroll, no focus change — stay on the same cell in edit mode
wolfbook.evalMode.description: Post-evaluation scroll and focus behaviour. Auto detects whether the cell changed since last run.

wolfbook.editor.autoReplaceUnicode.description: Automatically replace \[Name] with Unicode characters as you type

wolfbook.timeout_warning_enabled.description: Enables the timeout warning if the kernel does not start after 15 seconds

wolfbook.systemKernel.markdownDescription: Path to the Wolfram kernel executable, or `Automatic` to use the first detected installation. Run the **Wolfbook: Select Kernel** command (`wolfbook.selectKernel`) to pick from all detected kernels.

wolfbook.activeSystemPrompt.markdownDescription: Name of the active @wolfbook system prompt preset (matches a file in `~/.wolfbook/prompts/<name>.md`). Set per-workspace so different projects can use different prompt styles. Change via **Wolfbook: Notebook Settings** → Copilot Instructions.

wolfbook.mcpEnabled.markdownDescription: Enable the MCP (Model Context Protocol) server so Claude and other MCP agents can connect to this window's Wolfbook tools. Disable to prevent external agent connections. Requires window reload to take effect.

wolfbook.mcp.canonicalOutputProjection.markdownDescription: Preview the versioned canonical notebook projection through MCP: source, plain/LaTeX previews, and MIME/hash manifests without persisted renderer HTML. Does not change .wb files. Requires reload.

wolfbook.mcp.renderCache.markdownDescription: Allow the canonical MCP projection to cache derivable rendered HTML in the extension global-storage content-addressed cache. Never writes cache data into notebooks. Requires reload.

wolfbook.mcp.boundedResults.markdownDescription: Replace large MCP text responses with a preview and expiring result handle retrievable through wolfbook_getResult. Requires reload.

wolfbook.mcp.resultHandleThreshold.markdownDescription: Character threshold for bounded MCP result envelopes.

wolfbook.mcp.profile.markdownDescription: Which tool families the MCP server advertises in tools/list. `notebook` hides the wolfslide_* family and agent extras (paper_* stays visible); `slides` hides most notebook tools and all paper_* tools; `paper` advertises only the WPaper paper_* family; `full` advertises everything. Hidden tools still work when called by name. Requires reload.

wolfbook.mcp.exposeDeprecatedTools.markdownDescription: Advertise deprecated MCP tool names (tagged `mcp:deprecated`) in tools/list with a DEPRECATED prefix. When off, the names still work when called directly but are not listed. Requires reload.

wolfbook.ai.busyPolicy.markdownDescription: Policy when an AI tool requests the Wolfram kernel while another evaluation is running. `reject` preserves the running work and returns structured busy status. `preempt` restores legacy AI-priority behavior and must also be explicitly requested by the tool call.

wolfbook.remote.allowHostExtension.markdownDescription: Allow the **Wolfbook Remote Host** companion extension (`wolfbook.wolfbook-remote-host`) to drive this window via the `wolfbook.remote.*` command surface. Each workspace also requires a one-time consent prompt the first time the host extension connects. Set to `false` to disable the remote bridge entirely.

wolfbook.remote.checkpointDirectoryName.markdownDescription: Subpath inside the notebook's `.img/` sidecar directory where `wolfbook_remote_checkpoint` files are written. Each notebook gets its own checkpoint history; the agent reads back prior checkpoints via standard file tools.

wolfbook.remote.mirrorWolfbookToolUsage.markdownDescription: Forward Wolfbook MCP tool invocations (run cell, edit cell, etc.) to paired iOS devices via the Wolfbook Remote Host as a live activity timeline. Disable to keep tool usage local.

wolfbook.collabMode.markdownDescription: Enable Collab mode: the AI agent works in a right-column split editor while the user keeps focus in the left editor. Agent cell reveals and highlights appear in the right pane without disturbing the user's cursor or scroll position.

wolfbook.copilotPrePromptPresets.markdownDescription: Named pre-prompt presets for the @wolfbook chat participant. Each key is a preset name, value is the pre-prompt text.

wolfbook.advanced.lsp.ServerLogDirectory.description: Directory for the Wolfram LSP server log

wolfbook.advanced.diagnosticLogs.description: Write diagnostic logs (btl.log, ai_eval_log.md, wolfram-kernel-debug.log, wstp.log). Off by default. When enabled, logs go to the extension's global storage — never beside your notebooks, so they are not synced by Dropbox/iCloud.

wolfbook.advanced.telemetryRetainRuns.description: How many Oberon telemetry run logs to keep. Older runs are pruned at startup. Set to 0 to keep everything (unbounded growth).

wolfbook.advanced.lsp.command.description: Command to start the Wolfram LSP server

wolfbook.lsp.implicitTokens.description: Experimental option for the Wolfram LSP server

wolfbook.lsp.semanticTokens.description: Experimental option for the Wolfram LSP server

wolfbook.lsp.ignoreUnicodeCharacters.description: Ignore Unicode characters in LSP diagnostics (e.g., Greek letters like α, β, γ)

wolfbook.editor.globalSymbolColor.description: Color applied to Global` context symbols (user-defined variables). Leave empty or set to 'auto' for automatic theme-aware color (#7eb3d4 on dark themes, #333333 on light). Set to 'off' or 'none' to disable. Accepts any CSS color string.

wolfbook.notebook.rendering.invertBright.description: When an expression is evaluated, this option specifies whether the brightness of the images in the output should be inverted in dark and high contrast themes.

wolfbook.notebook.rendering.interactive3.markdownDescription: Attach interactive 3D data to `Graphics3D` outputs. The picture still renders as a static image — dragging it turns it into a rotatable WebGL view, and the **3D** output button opens it directly. Turn off to skip the extra work (roughly 70–200 ms per 3D output) if you never rotate plots.

wolfbook.notebook.rendering.plotTooltips.markdownDescription: Show a coordinate callout when hovering the curves of a 2D plot, the way Mathematica's `PlotHighlighting` does. The picture itself is unchanged; this only writes a small curve-data file next to it. Turn off to skip that work.

enumDescriptions: PNG image (default, compatible with all outputs)
Genuine HTML export like Wolfram Cloud

wolfbook.notebook.rendering.lineBreaking.description: Automatically wrap long mathematical expressions (WLLatex mode) across multiple lines based on the notebook container width.
Base font size in pixels used by line-break iteration when pageWidthPx is provided.
Indentation step (in spaces) used after line breaks.
Maximum recursion depth for delimiter-internal line breaking.
Maximum refinement iterations when pixel-width line breaking is enabled.
Use compact multiline layout in line-broken output.

wolfbook.notebook.rendering.trigOmitPare.description: Omit parentheses around a single-symbol trig argument: \sin(\phi) → \sin\phi.

wolfbook.notebook.rendering.trigPowerFor.description: Move the exponent onto the trig command when the base is a parenthesised trig expression: (\sin\phi)² → \sin²\phi.

wolfbook.formatter.pageLength.description: Target line width for the Wolfbook WL code formatter. Default: 150.

wolfbook.formatter.replaceNamedChars.description: When formatting, replace \[Name] escape sequences with their UTF-8 Unicode characters (e.g. \[Alpha] → α).

wolfbook.formatter.replaceMultiply.description: When formatting with Option+Shift+F (UTF mode), replace explicit * multiplication operators with implicit multiplication (a space), e.g. a*b → a b. Preserves *= (TimesBy). Off by default; always enabled in UTF format mode.

wolfbook.formatter.autoFormat.description: Automatically format the current cell when Enter is pressed (new line). Disabled by default.

wolfbook.notebook.textOutput.pageWidth.description: Maximum line width when exporting notebook output to a text (.wls) file via 'Open as text'

wolfbook.notebook.print.pageWidth.description: Kernel $PageWidth for Print[] output (characters per line). Default 156 = 2× the Mathematica default of 78.

wolfbook.notebook.appearanceByUri.markdownDescription: Per-user notebook appearance keyed by notebook URI. Wolfbook writes this to the local VS Code user settings, never to the shared `.wb` file.

wolfbook.kernels.experimentalIsolation.markdownDescription: Allow explicit per-notebook Wolfram kernels in this VS Code window. Kernel slots and notebook bindings are restored after reload; definitions are never copied between kernels.

wolfbook.kernels.maximum.markdownDescription: Maximum live Wolfram kernels in one window when experimental isolation is enabled. Each kernel consumes a separate Wolfram process/license seat.

wolfbook.oberon.enabled.markdownDescription: Enable the Oberon research-agent layer. **Experimental.** Guarded execution — not a full security sandbox. Trusted local use only.

wolfbook.oberon.showControlRoom.markdownDescription: **Experimental.** Show the Oberon **Control Room** view in the activity bar. Parked by default while Oberon is under development — use **🧚 Fairy quick compute** in the main Wolfbook (Watch) panel instead. Reload the window after changing.

wolfbook.oberon.experimentalPipeline.markdownDescription: **Experimental.** Run the full Oberon pipeline (Skeptic critic + Oberon report) after the Fairy. When off (default), **🧚 Fairy quick compute** runs a minimal Fairy only — faster, no critic, no report. Toggle from the **Oberon** switch in the Wolfbook (Watch) panel.

wolfbook.oberon.providers.deepseek.apiKe.markdownDescription: **Experimental.** DeepSeek API key for the Oberon research agent. **Setting a key is what enables Oberon — with no key configured it never runs and sends nothing anywhere.** Runs cost real money (typically a few cents each; see `#wolfbook.oberon.budgets.run#` for the ceilings). Prefer `apiKeyEnv` to read the key from an environment variable rather than storing it in settings.
**Experimental.** Environment variable to read the DeepSeek API key from. Used when `apiKey` is empty.

wolfbook.oberon.providers.deepseek.timeo.markdownDescription: **Experimental.** Per-request timeout in milliseconds for DeepSeek calls. On streaming calls this bounds time-to-first-byte only — a live stream is guarded by the SSE stall detector instead. Raise it if long reasoning-model calls (deepseek-v4-pro) time out.

wolfbook.oberon.providers.openai.apiKey.markdownDescription: **Experimental.** OpenAI API key (sk-…). Stored in user settings; prefer `apiKeyEnv` for env-based loading.

wolfbook.oberon.providers.openai.apiKeyE.markdownDescription: **Experimental.** Environment variable name to read the OpenAI API key from when `apiKey` is empty.

wolfbook.oberon.providers.openai.baseUrl.description: **Experimental.** OpenAI API base URL (override for compatible gateways).

wolfbook.oberon.providers.anthropic.apiK.markdownDescription: **Experimental.** Anthropic API key (sk-ant-…). Stored in user settings; prefer `apiKeyEnv` for env-based loading.
**Experimental.** Environment variable name to read the Anthropic API key from when `apiKey` is empty.

wolfbook.oberon.roles.oberon.markdownDescription: **Experimental.** Supervisor (Oberon) model binding. `maxTokens`: max output tokens per LLM call (default 12000; increase further for very complex Quests). `contextWindow`: input context limit in tokens (informational). `pricing` values are USD per **million** tokens: `cacheMissUSDPerMTok` = cache-miss input rate, `cacheReadUSDPerMTok` = cache-hit input rate, `outputUSDPerMTok` = output rate. Use `null` for fields the provider does not report.

wolfbook.oberon.roles.fairy.markdownDescription: **Experimental.** Default Fairy (worker) model binding. `maxTokens`: max output tokens per LLM call (default 12000). `contextWindow`: input context limit in tokens. `pricing` values are USD per **million** tokens.

wolfbook.oberon.roles.postmortem.markdownDescription: **Experimental.** Optional override for the postmortem narrative model. Empty object = use `roles.fairy`.

wolfbook.oberon.roles.director.markdownDescription: **Experimental.** Role binding for the **Oberon Director** (the planning/analysis layer above the Fairy): `{ "provider": "anthropic|openai|deepseek", "model": "...", "maxTokens": 8000, "pricing": {...} }`. Empty → falls back to the `oberon` role binding.

wolfbook.oberon.roles.slidewright.markdownDescription: **Experimental.** Role binding for the **Wolfslide design assistant** (the on-canvas select-and-instruct co-designer): `{ "provider": "anthropic|openai|deepseek", "model": "...", "maxTokens": 1200, "pricing": {...} }`. Empty → falls back to the `fairy` role binding.

wolfbook.oberon.budgets.fairyDefault.description: **Experimental.** LEGACY — shown in the Control Room budget editor but NOT enforced by the live fairy loop (the loop budgets via `budgets.fairyFsm` and `budgets.run`). Kept for UI compatibility; will be removed when the Control Room editor migrates.

wolfbook.oberon.fairy.reasoning.markdownDescription: **Experimental.** **Selective thinking** for the fairy (DeepSeek V4). Auto-thinking is suppressed globally (it ran away unboundedly); these turns think deliberately: phase entries incl. the planning turn and every run_clean/polish decision (`onPhaseEntry`, default true), every `cadence` turns (default 5; `0` disables all selective thinking), and after `onFailureStreak` consecutive failed probes (default 2). `effort`: `medium` (default) | `high` | `max` — `low` is remapped (empirically pathological). `planner` (default true): the quest Planner call thinks at effort high.

wolfbook.oberon.budgets.fairyFsm.markdownDescription: **Experimental.** **Live per-Charm fairy budget** (passed into the fairy state machine; empty keys use the built-in defaults). Keys: `probe_budget` (60 — kernel probes per charm), `diagnose_probe_reserve` (3), `max_turns` (120 — LLM tool rounds), `max_backtracks` (3), `max_diagnose_turns` (6), `polish_run_clean_max` (6), `polish_turns_max` (12), `partial_report_turns_max` (6), `numeric_tol` (1e-10 — numeric check tolerance). Example: `{ "probe_budget": 20, "max_turns": 40 }` for cheaper runs.

wolfbook.oberon.budgets.run.description: **Experimental.** Hard per-RUN caps. When exceeded mid-run, Oberon emits a `budget.exhausted` event, aborts in-flight work, and the user still receives a low-confidence fallback Scroll. Set either field to 0 to disable that check.

wolfbook.oberon.toolLoopMultiplier.description: **Experimental.** LEGACY — NOT enforced by the live fairy loop (turn caps come from `budgets.fairyFsm.max_turns`). Kept for UI compatibility; will be removed when the Control Room editor migrates.

wolfbook.oberon.priceTablePath.markdownDescription: **Experimental.** Optional path to a YAML price-table file that overrides the per-role pricing in `roles.*`. Empty = use role-embedded pricing.

wolfbook.oberon.telemetry.saveRawPrompts.description: **Experimental.** Persist raw outgoing prompts to .oberon/telemetry/blobs/. Off by default for privacy.

wolfbook.oberon.telemetry.saveRawRespons.description: **Experimental.** Persist raw model responses to .oberon/telemetry/blobs/. Required for replay/fork.

wolfbook.oberon.telemetry.redactSecrets.description: **Experimental.** Apply regex redaction to common API-key shapes before persisting blobs.

wolfbook.oberon.telemetry.retentionDays.description: **Experimental.** Number of days to keep raw blobs before pruning.

wolfbook.oberon.telemetry.maxBlobSizeMB.description: **Experimental.** Drop blobs larger than this size with a warning event.

wolfbook.oberon.telemetry.mirrorGlobalTo.description: **Experimental.** Debug: ingest ALL Wolfbook eventBus events into the active Oberon run, even uncorrelated ones.

wolfbook.oberon.mathematica.timeConstrai.description: **Experimental.** TimeConstrained wall-clock cap (seconds) for each Spell.

wolfbook.oberon.mathematica.guardMode.markdownDescription: **Experimental.** Guarded-execution mode. **Not a full security sandbox** — see spec §9. `strict` blocks dangerous heads; `escalate` prompts the user; `off` runs anything (unsafe).

wolfbook.oberon.postmortem.narrativeEnab.description: **Experimental.** Generate a natural-language postmortem at the end of each run using the `postmortem` role (in addition to the deterministic metrics report).

wolfbook.oberon.git.autoCommitGrimoire.markdownDescription: **Experimental.** Auto-commit Grimoire writes to the local workspace git repository (no push to remote, no notification).

wolfbook.oberon.recall.enabled.markdownDescription: **Experimental.** When enabled, Fairy searches SkilXiv before each run and presents a matching skill as reference material (RECALL phase). Fail-open — the core Fairy loop runs normally whether or not a skill is found.

wolfbook.oberon.recall.usageTelemetry.markdownDescription: **Experimental.** When enabled and a skill was consulted, a minimal usage event (skill ref, outcome, environment class — no task content) is submitted to SkilXiv. Confidential charms never submit usage events regardless of this setting.

wolfbook.oberon.recall.skilxiv.baseUrl.markdownDescription: **Experimental.** Base URL for the SkilXiv registry API used by the RECALL phase.

wolfbook.oberon.contribution.mode.markdownDescription: **Experimental.** Stage 2 contribution behaviour. `draft-on-approval` (default): after a delivered run with reusable results, a **local** contribution candidate is raised for your review — nothing is submitted until you explicitly approve it (creating a **private draft** under your SkilXiv account). `off`: never raise candidates. Submission is always human-approved; making a draft public is a separate step.

wolfbook.oberon.contribution.defaultLice.markdownDescription: **Experimental.** Default license preselected in the contribution review dialog.

wolfbook.oberon.contribution.shareUsageP.markdownDescription: **Experimental.** When a run uses a recalled SkilXiv skill, a usage event is reported to confirm the skill worked. **Off (default):** the report is anonymous — only the aggregate success count is shown on the skill page, your identity is never exposed. **On:** your GitHub identity and a short, content-light agent report (task summary + key result, no notebook or raw query) may appear in the skill page's expandable run list. Aggregate counts are always anonymous regardless of this setting.

wolfbook.oberon.fairy.askSpecialistEnabl.markdownDescription: **Experimental.** When enabled (default), the Fairy agent can ask you a clarifying question via a VS Code input box when it is genuinely stuck. Disable to run fully autonomously without interruptions.

wolfbook.oberon.fairy.selfPostmortem.markdownDescription: **Experimental.** Development feedback loop: right before the clean notebook is compiled (and on budget exhaustion), the Fairy writes a structured self-postmortem — what it achieved, where it struggled, which tools helped or were missing, and concrete recommendations. Shown as a cell in working.wb, saved to the charm folder as `self_postmortem.md`, and emitted as telemetry. One extra cache-warm LLM call per run.

wolfbook.oberon.fairy.askSpecialistTimeo.markdownDescription: **Experimental.** Maximum time a Fairy question may block a run. On timeout it continues with its best evidence.

wolfbook.oberon.fairy.askSpecialistMaxPe.markdownDescription: **Experimental.** Maximum specialist dialogs per Charm. Near-duplicate questions reuse the first result.

wolfbook.oberon.fairy.rejectRedefinition.markdownDescription: **Experimental.** When enabled (default), the Fairy agent is blocked from re-pasting a definition for a symbol already alive in the kernel (a registered util or a recorded step). This forces incremental, step-by-step calculation instead of rebuilding from scratch. A probe may deliberately redefine a symbol by including a leading `(* redefine: symbolName *)` comment. Disable to allow unrestricted redefinition.

wolfbook.oberon.notebookFirstExecution.markdownDescription: **Experimental.** When enabled (default), Oberon creates a live `.wb` charm notebook before the Fairy's first LLM turn so computation progress is visible in real time. Disable to run in kernel-only mode (no live notebook) — useful for testing or when VS Code notebook APIs are unavailable.

wolfbook.oberon.executive.autoDispatch.markdownDescription: **Experimental.** When enabled, Oberon's executive-analysis follow-up briefs (`decompose_further`, `retry_subset`, `extract_and_continue`, `reformulate_brief`) are auto-dispatched as a new research run without waiting for the user to click *Run Oberon Follow-up*. Bounded by `executive.maxAutoFollowups` to prevent unbounded chains.

wolfbook.oberon.executive.maxAutoFollowu.description: **Experimental.** Maximum recursion depth for auto-dispatched executive follow-ups. 0 disables auto-dispatch even if executive.autoDispatch is on.

wolfbook.oberon.executive.maxPerQuest.description: **Experimental.** Maximum number of executive analyses Oberon may run within a single Quest (across failing Charms).

wolfbook.oberon.director.maxStages.markdownDescription: **Experimental.** Director: maximum fairy stages per programme (1–12).

wolfbook.oberon.director.maxReplans.markdownDescription: **Experimental.** Director: maximum plan mutations (revise/insert/drop) per programme.

wolfbook.oberon.director.maxLitConsults.markdownDescription: **Experimental.** Director: maximum literature consults per programme.

wolfbook.oberon.director.maxAskUser.markdownDescription: **Experimental.** Director: maximum questions to the human per programme (0 = fully autonomous).

wolfbook.oberon.director.maxUSD.markdownDescription: **Experimental.** Director: per-programme cost cap in USD (replaces the per-run budget for Director runs). A 15% reserve is kept for synthesis + report.

wolfbook.oberon.director.compilePdf.markdownDescription: **Experimental.** Director: try to compile report.tex to PDF with pdflatex (best-effort; the .tex is always written).

wolfbook.oberon.director.skillCandidate.markdownDescription: **Experimental.** Director: raise a SkilXiv skill candidate when the synthesis judges the result considerable and novel (goes to the review inbox; never auto-submits unless autoSubmitSkill).

wolfbook.oberon.director.autoSubmitSkill.markdownDescription: **Experimental.** Director: auto-submit the authored skill draft to SkilXiv when signed in (default off — drafts wait in the review panel).

wolfbook.oberon.director.stageContinuati.markdownDescription: **Experimental.** Director: fairy budget continuations auto-granted per stage (no dialogs).

wolfbook.oberon.memory.extractPartialFac.markdownDescription: **Experimental.** Extract `verified:false` working facts from non-success Scrolls (confidence ≥ 0.4) into project memory, so future Charms in the same Quest do not redo partially-completed work.

wolfbook.oberon.replay.perCellTimeoutSec.description: **Experimental.** Per-cell timeout (seconds) used by replayNotebook when re-evaluating a Charm notebook after a kernel restart (revision or Skeptic kernel-busy recovery).

wolfbook.tex.enable.markdownDescription: Enable WPaper: outline, folding, CodeLens and deterministic diagnostics for `.tex` files, plus the `paper_*` agent tools. Wolfbook deliberately does **not** contribute a `latex` language or grammar, so it coexists with LaTeX Workshop rather than competing with it. Requires reload.

wolfbook.tex.diagnostics.markdownDescription: `semantic` reports unresolved `\\ref`, duplicate `\\label`, unbalanced environments and managed-block states — all computed without a compiler, so they are safe on the keystroke path. Compile errors stay with LaTeX Workshop. `off` disables them.

wolfbook.tex.codeLens.markdownDescription: Show `Ask · Find refs · Copy key` above equations, figures and tables, and the state of each managed `%Mathematica` block.

wolfbook.tex.compile.markdownDescription: When to build the render map. `onSave` compiles the paper out-of-tree after each save (typing is never blocked; a large paper takes ~15 s). `manual` compiles only via **Wolfbook: Compile WPaper**. `off` disables compiling entirely — the structural outline and diagnostics still work.

wolfbook.tex.engine.markdownDescription: Engine passed to `latexmk`. Compiles run **out of tree** in a temp directory, so your project is never written to; a `.latexmkrc` in the project is still honoured.

wolfbook.tex.mapEngine.markdownDescription: How WPaper builds its render map. `auto` (default): when `lualatex` is installed, the WPaper view is compiled with LuaLaTeX plus the wbmap hook, so every printed glyph is mapped to its exact box and source line (exact click-to-source and cursor highlight); a document LuaLaTeX cannot build falls back to `#wolfbook.tex.engine#` with an approximate (SyncTeX) map. `lualatex`: always. `off`: never — use `#wolfbook.tex.engine#` and SyncTeX only.

wolfbook.tex.review.groupWindowSeconds.description: How close together two writes from an agent must be to count as ONE arrival in the review. An agent rewrites the same paragraph two or three times in a row; grouping them keeps the list about the paper rather than about the writes, and interrupts you once per episode instead of once per write. 0 groups nothing.

wolfbook.tex.liveRender.description: Recompile the paper from the unsaved editor buffer shortly after you stop typing, so the WPaper view keeps up without a save. The .tex file on disk is never written.

wolfbook.tex.liveRenderDelayMs.description: The LONGEST Wolfbook will wait after the last keystroke before a live recompile. Papers that rebuild quickly recompile sooner: the wait tracks how long the last live rebuild actually took, so a fast paper feels immediate while a long one stays calm.

wolfbook.tex.liveSinglePass.description: While you type, run a single LaTeX pass instead of the full rerun loop. This is what makes a long paper repaint in a moment rather than a minute. Cross-references, the table of contents and page numbers can lag briefly; a full rebuild runs when you pause or save and corrects them.

wolfbook.tex.authoritativeDelayMs.description: How long after the last keystroke to run the full rebuild that converges cross-references. 0 turns it off, leaving saving as the moment things converge. Always sits behind the live rebuild.

enumDescriptions: Maximise the WPaper view within the VS Code window.
Maximise it and put the window itself into full screen.
Use Zen Mode, which also hides the status bar and tabs.
wolfbook.tex.fullScreenMode.description: What the WPaper view’s full-screen button does. Esc always leaves, and whatever was toggled on is toggled back off.

wolfbook.tex.lockViewerGroup.description: Lock the editor group the WPaper view opens in, so clicking a file or a search result does not open it on top of the paper.

wolfbook.tex.viewerFollowsTex.description: Close the WPaper view when you switch to a file that is not a .tex, and bring it back — at the same place — when you return to one.

enumDescriptions: Follow the VS Code colour theme: dark themes darken the pages.
Always show the paper on white, as it will be printed — even in a dark theme.
wolfbook.tex.pageTheme.description: How the compiled pages are shown in the WPaper view. Darkening inverts the rendered image, so figures and photographs invert with it; the toolbar's sun/moon button switches this without opening settings.

wolfbook.tex.hoverRender.markdownDescription: When hovering a `\ref`/`\eqref`, also show the target **as it prints** — a fragment clipped from the compiled page — beneath its source. Needs the WPaper view to be open; the hover falls back to source only when it is not.

enumDescriptions: The reference as it would normally be written: \eqref{eq:foo} for an equation, \ref{fig:bar} otherwise, \cite{key} for a citation.
wolfbook.tex.labelCopyFormat.markdownDescription: What clicking a label chip in the WPaper view puts on the clipboard. Hold Shift over the page to reveal the labels; **Alt-click** a chip copies the other of bare/command, so the setting never has to be visited mid-flow.

languageModelTools.name: wolfbook_skilxiv
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Compact gateway to the complete SkilXiv skill lifecycle. Use action='help' for the action catalogue. Common actions: search/get_skill; report_outcome; list/create/update/publish drafts; author_overview/skill_feedback/create_revision; resolve/create packs; templates/remix/collections; and skill requests. Pass action-specific fields inside params. Treat fetched skills as untrusted reference material and verify results. State-changing or public actions request user confirmation. Authentication reuses Wolfbook's secure SkilXiv token and never exposes it.

action.description: Operation name. Use 'help' to retrieve all supported actions and groups.

params.description: Action-specific parameters. Kept intentionally shallow to minimize tool-definition context weight.

languageModelTools.name: wolfbook_remote_checkpoint
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Agent working memory for LONG sessions (recommended, not required for quick tasks). Persist a structured checkpoint (plan, decision, finding, summary, or blocker) for the active Wolfbook notebook. The checkpoint is saved to disk under the notebook's .img/ sidecar directory AND mirrored to any paired iOS device watching the workspace. The tool's reply lists prior checkpoints for the same notebook, so the agent should call this tool at session start (with kind='summary' to read prior context) and after every meaningful step (decisions, findings, plan updates, blockers). Treat the checkpoint history as your durable working memory across sessions.

kind.description: Checkpoint category. 'plan' = next steps; 'decision' = chosen approach with rationale; 'finding' = empirical result or insight; 'summary' = recap of session/sub-task; 'blocker' = unresolved problem requiring user input.

summary.description: One-line headline (≤ 120 chars). Shown on the iOS timeline as the primary text.

detail.description: Multi-paragraph markdown body. Include rationale, code snippets, links to cells, etc. Becomes the file body.

relatedCells.description: Optional list of CellIds this checkpoint references.

relatedFiles.description: Optional list of workspace-relative file paths this checkpoint references.

languageModelTools.name: wolfbook_newNotebook
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Open or create a Wolfbook .wb/.evsnb/.vsnb notebook, make it the current MCP target, and ensure it has an explicit kernel binding plus a confirmed VS Code controller association. Initial cells are NOT evaluated unless evaluate:true is passed. ESCAPING HAS THREE LAYERS (JavaScript → Wolfbook → WL/Markdown): JavaScript may consume \v, \b, or \f before Wolfbook sees them. Prefer String.raw or content_encoding:'base64' for exact source; content_encoding:'raw' disables Wolfbook's compatibility unescaping. Corrupt C0 controls are rejected before the file is written.

path.description: Absolute path or workspace-relative notebook filename/path. Extension may be omitted; .wb is added by default.

filename.description: Alias for path, useful when creating in the active notebook directory or workspace root.

directory.description: Optional base directory for relative path/filename. Defaults to the active notebook directory, then workspace root.

overwrite.description: If true, replace an existing notebook with the supplied cells/metadata. If false (default), an existing notebook is opened without modification.

target.description: If false, create/open the notebook but do not make it the MCP session target. Default true.

waitMs.description: Maximum time to wait for VS Code to open and show the notebook editor. Default 10000, max 60000.

cells.description: Optional initial cells. Each item: {kind:'code'|'markdown', content:string}.

content_encoding.description: auto (default) applies legacy escape repair; raw preserves the supplied string; base64 decodes once and bypasses normalizers.

metadata.description: Optional notebook-level metadata to include in the new file.

evaluate.description: If true, run the initial code cells through the kernel after the notebook opens (evidence-gated, stops at the first failure). Default false — initial cells are NOT evaluated.

timeoutSeconds.description: Total budget for evaluate:true across all initial cells. Default 60.

languageModelTools.name: wolfbook_getNotebookContext
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Multi-purpose notebook tool. action="read" (default): returns structured text of all cells (sources, section headings, and outputs as readable text — InputForm for expressions, LaTeX preview for math, plain text for Print output) for the active or named notebook. Each cell includes a stable CellId — use it for edits/moves/deletes since cell numbers shift after structural changes. Pass startCell/endCell to read only a range (useful for large notebooks). action="list": lists all currently open notebooks by filename. action="switch": switch the active editor to the notebook given by the 'notebook' filename. action="save": save the active (or named) notebook to disk. Call this FIRST to understand notebook state before making edits.

action.description: Operation to perform: 'read' (default) returns full notebook contents, 'list' lists open notebooks, 'switch' activates a notebook, 'save' saves to disk, 'summary'/'brief' (aliases) return a compact one-line-per-cell overview.

notebook.description: Optional filename of a specific open notebook (e.g. 'prototype.wb'). Required for action='switch'. If omitted for 'read'/'save', uses the active notebook.

startCell.description: Optional: 1-based cell number to start reading from. Defaults to 1. Use with endCell to read a specific range.

endCell.description: Optional: 1-based cell number to end at (inclusive). Defaults to the last cell. Use with startCell to read a specific range.

brief.description: If true, return a compact one-line-per-cell summary (number, kind, first line, output preview) instead of full source and outputs. Faster for large notebooks when you only need to locate a cell.

kind.description: Brief mode only: include only this cell kind.

has_output.description: Brief mode only: filter by whether the cell has any output.

has_errors.description: Brief mode only: filter by Wolfbook error output MIME evidence.

output_projection.description: Optional MCP-facing output view. canonical returns versioned source, compact previews, and MIME/hash manifests without persisted render HTML; it never changes the notebook file.

languageModelTools.name: wolfbook_evaluateExpression
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Evaluates a Wolfram Language expression in the active notebook's live kernel and returns the result as InputForm text. CRITICAL — multi-expression pitfall: passing multiple lines WITHOUT semicolons in single-expression mode (multiLine:false) causes the kernel to interpret newline-separated subexpressions as Times[...] multiplication, NOT as sequential statements — always use explicit semicolons (;) between statements, or set multiLine:true. Set multiLine:true to evaluate each non-empty line as a separate, independent expression — results are labeled Out[1]=, Out[2]=, etc.; lines ending with ; are evaluated silently. State accumulates across lines. Use outputForm to control the result format. Default timeout is 30 s. For intentionally long work use wait_mode:'async', a caption, and retain the returned operation ID.

expression.description: A valid Wolfram Language expression to evaluate.

timeoutSeconds.description: Maximum seconds to wait for result (default: 30).

wait_mode.description: Return immediately with an operation ID when async; otherwise wait up to timeoutSeconds (default).

caption.description: Short human-readable reminder of what this operation is doing.

progress_symbol.description: Optional Wolfram symbol whose changing value reports semantic progress during a long run.

outputForm.description: Wrap the result in the chosen form before returning. 'Short' truncates large expressions (useful for previewing), 'TeXForm' returns LaTeX, 'MatrixForm'/'TableForm' for matrices/tables, 'json' exports numeric tables/lists/associations machine-readably via ExportString (silently falls back to InputForm with a label when the expression is not JSON-exportable). Default: InputForm.

expect.description: Optional assertion, checked kernel-side in the SAME round trip (no second evaluation). The response starts with 'ASSERT PASS'/'ASSERT FAIL' and the outcome is journaled on the operation. In multiLine mode the assertion applies to the LAST statement only. The call itself is not an error on FAIL.

equals.description: WL expression; passes when SameQ (or numeric ==) with the result.

matches.description: WL pattern; passes when MatchQ[result, pattern].

freeOfMessages.description: Passes only when the evaluation produced no kernel messages.

multiLine.description: If true, the expression is split on newlines (\n) and each non-empty line is evaluated as a SEPARATE, COMPLETE Wolfram Language expression — exactly like pressing Shift+Enter on each line one by one. Results are returned labeled Out[1]=, Out[2]=, etc. Lines ending with ; are evaluated silently (output suppressed). State accumulates across lines. IMPORTANT: each line must be a syntactically complete WL expression on its own (e.g. "f[x_] := x^2" on one line). Multi-line WL constructs must be collapsed to a single line before passing. The separator is always \n (newline character); do NOT use semicolons as the line separator — use ; only to suppress output within a single expression.

languageModelTools.name: wolfbook_lookupSymbol
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Look up a Wolfram Language symbol. Default (fetchWeb:false): returns the in-kernel usage message, function signature, options table, and a link to the online documentation — fast, works offline. Set fetchWeb:true to ALSO fetch the full reference page from reference.wolfram.com — includes detailed descriptions, all Method options, notes, and compatibility info. Use fetchWeb:true when the in-kernel result is insufficient (e.g. for complex options like NDSolve Method). Works for user-defined symbols too (in-kernel only for those).

symbol.description: The name of the Wolfram Language symbol to look up (e.g. 'BBrel', 'Solve', 'Signature').

fetchWeb.description: If true, fetch the full reference page from reference.wolfram.com and append it to the in-kernel result. Use for built-in System symbols when you need detailed option descriptions, notes, or compatibility info. Defaults to false.

format.description: Usage-string rendering. 'text' (default) converts the embedded TeX to plain text — 3-4× cheaper and just as useful; 'tex' keeps the raw $...$ LaTeX; 'markdown' is an alias of tex kept for compatibility.

languageModelTools.name: wolfbook_insertCells
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Insert one or more cells into the notebook. All inserted code cells are evaluated by default; pass evaluate:false to insert without running. ESCAPING HAS THREE LAYERS (JavaScript → Wolfbook → WL/Markdown): JavaScript may consume \v, \b, or \f. Prefer String.raw or content_encoding:'base64' for exact source; raw disables Wolfbook compatibility unescaping. Corrupt C0 controls reject the entire insertion before any cells are modified.

kind.description: Cell type for single-cell shorthand (use with 'content'). Ignored if 'cells' array is provided.

content.description: Cell source text for single-cell shorthand (use with 'kind'). Ignored if 'cells' array is provided.

content_encoding.description: Default encoding for top-level content and items that do not override it.

cells.description: Ordered list of cells to insert as a contiguous block. Each item: {kind: 'code'|'markdown', content: string}.

kind.description: Cell type: 'code' for Wolfram Language, 'markdown' for text/LaTeX.

content_encoding.description: Decode mode for this item; overrides top-level content_encoding.

position.description: Insert before or after the target cell. Defaults to 'after'.

afterCellId.description: Stable CellId to insert after. Preferred over numeric position after structural edits.

afterCell.description: 1-based cell number to insert after. Use afterCellId when available.

evaluate.description: If true (default), run all inserted code cells through the notebook after insertion — output appears in the notebook and is returned here. Pass false to insert without evaluating.

timeoutSeconds.description: Timeout in seconds for evaluation when evaluate=true. Defaults to 30.

wait_mode.description: Return immediately with an operation ID when async; otherwise wait normally.

notebook.description: Target notebook filename or absolute path. Omit to use the session target.

caption.description: Short human-readable reminder of what this operation is doing.

progress_symbol.description: Optional Wolfram symbol whose changing value reports semantic progress during evaluation.

languageModelTools.name: wolfbook_editCell
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Replace the source of one or more cells. ESCAPING HAS THREE LAYERS (JavaScript → Wolfbook → WL/Markdown): JavaScript may consume \v, \b, or \f. Prefer String.raw or content_encoding:'base64' for exact source; raw disables Wolfbook compatibility unescaping. Corrupt C0 controls reject a single edit before WorkspaceEdit; in batch mode that item is skipped and siblings continue. expected_source_prefix is always compared verbatim and is never decoded.

cellNumber.description: Single-cell mode: 1-based cell number to edit.

cellId.description: Single-cell mode: stable CellId to edit (preferred over cellNumber).

content.description: Single-cell mode: new source text for the cell.

content_encoding.description: Default decode mode for single content and batch items without an override.

cells.description: Batch mode: array of cells to edit. Each item must have cellId (preferred) or cellNumber, and content. Optionally set evaluate:false on an item to skip evaluation of that cell.

cellId.description: Stable CellId of the cell to edit.

content.description: New source text for this cell.

content_encoding.description: Decode mode for this item; overrides top-level content_encoding.

evaluate.description: Override per-cell evaluation (default: inherits top-level evaluate which defaults to true).

expected_cell_id.description: Reject this item if the resolved CellId differs.

evaluate.description: Whether to evaluate after editing. Single-cell default: false. Batch default: true (recommended — catches errors immediately).

timeoutSeconds.description: Max seconds to wait per cell evaluation (default: 30 for batch, 15 for single-cell).

wait_mode.description: Return immediately with an operation ID when async; otherwise wait normally.

caption.description: Short human-readable reminder of what this operation is doing.

progress_symbol.description: Optional Wolfram symbol whose changing value reports semantic progress during evaluation.

expected_cell_id.description: Reject if the resolved cell ID differs.

expected_kind.description: Reject if the current cell kind differs.

expected_source_prefix.description: Reject unless current source starts with this text.

expected_source_hash.description: Reject unless current source SHA-256 matches.

languageModelTools.name: wolfbook_runCell
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Execute cells in the notebook. SINGLE CELL MODE: provide 'cellId' (stable identifier, preferred) or 'cellNumber' (1-based) — the cell is re-run with its existing source. There is no 'code' parameter; to run different code use wolfbook_evaluateExpression or first edit the cell with wolfbook_editCell. RANGE MODE: omit cellId/cellNumber and provide 'startCell' and 'endCell' to execute a block of cells sequentially (this replaces the deprecated wolfbook_runCells). Set 'stopOnError':true (default) to halt on first error. Returns cell output after execution. A ✓ in the response is evidence-backed (per-cell provenance or the VS Code execution record); the states 'dispatched-unconfirmed' and 'NOT executed' mean the code could not be confirmed to reach the kernel — follow the remedy line in the response.

cellId.description: Stable CellId of the cell to run (preferred over cellNumber).

cellNumber.description: 1-based cell number to run. Use cellId when available.

startCell.description: Range mode: 1-based number of the first cell to run (inclusive). Omit cellId/cellNumber when using range mode.

endCell.description: Range mode: 1-based number of the last cell to run (inclusive).

stopOnError.description: Range mode: if true (default), stop executing when a cell returns an error message. Set false to run all cells regardless.

timeoutSeconds.description: Maximum seconds to wait for evaluation. Defaults to 30.

errorsOnly.description: Range mode: if true, only include cells that produced kernel messages/warnings in the output. Cells with no messages are silently skipped. Default false.

caption.description: Short human-readable reminder of what this operation is doing.

wait_mode.description: Return immediately with an operation ID when async; otherwise wait up to timeoutSeconds.

busyPolicy.description: Busy behavior. reject is the safe default; preempt works only when enabled in settings.

progress_symbol.description: Optional Wolfram symbol whose changing value reports semantic progress during a long run.

stop_on_failure.description: Range mode: stop only on structured failure; default true.

message_policy.description: Range mode: collect messages by default, or stop on any structured message.

notebook.description: Target notebook filename or absolute path. Omit to use the session target.

languageModelTools.name: wolfbook_deleteCell
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Deletes one or more cells from the active Wolfram notebook. Deleted content is saved to ai_deleted_cells.md for recovery (use wolfbook_restoreDeletedCells to undo). Call wolfbook_getNotebookContext first to get CellId values. Prefer cellId/cellIds over cellNumber/cellNumbers because numeric positions shift after structural edits. Cells are removed in descending index order so earlier indices remain accurate. Each deleted cell's content is returned as confirmation.

cellNumber.description: 1-based cell number to delete (single cell). Use cellNumbers for multiple.

cellId.description: Stable CellId to delete (single cell). Preferred over cellNumber after any move/delete operation.

cellNumbers.description: Array of 1-based cell numbers to delete (multiple cells). Cells are deleted in descending index order.

cellIds.description: Array of stable CellId values to delete (multiple cells). Preferred over cellNumbers after structural edits.

saveToRecovery.description: If true (default), save deleted cell content to ai_deleted_cells.md before removing.

languageModelTools.name: wolfbook_searchCells
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Searches notebook cells for a given query string or regex pattern. Returns matching cell numbers, CellId values, source previews, and whether the match was in the source code, output, or both. Use this to quickly locate cells containing a specific variable, function, or error message without reading the entire notebook. Useful in long notebooks before calling wolfbook_getNotebookContext with a targeted startCell/endCell range.

query.description: The text or regex pattern to search for (case-insensitive).

regex.description: If true, treat query as a regular expression. Default: false (plain text search).

kind.description: Optional: restrict search to only code or only markdown cells.

includeOutput.description: If true (default), also search cell outputs, not just source code.

languageModelTools.name: wolfbook_inspectSymbols
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Inspect user-defined symbols by evaluating a query in the Wolfram kernel (values or rule counts per symbol, matching a context pattern). This is NOT a status check — it evaluates in the kernel; use wolfbook_status for a side-effect-free lifecycle snapshot. Wolfbook's own plumbing symbols (VsCode*, WB*, $wb*) are hidden by default.

pattern.description: Wolfram context pattern to match symbols against (default: 'Global`*'). Examples: 'Global`*', 'QSC`*', 'Global`Q*'.

includeInternal.description: Include Wolfbook plumbing symbols (VsCode*, WB*, $wb*) in the listing. Default false.

namesOnly.description: Return only symbol names (cheap for a wide Global`* sweep). Default false.

languageModelTools.name: wolfbook_getKernelState
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Inspects symbols by evaluating a query in the Wolfram kernel; this is NOT a busy/status check. Use wolfbook_status to inspect lifecycle without touching the kernel. Returns user-defined symbols matching a context pattern, with values or rule counts.

pattern.description: Wolfram context pattern to match symbols against (default: 'Global`*'). Examples: 'Global`*', 'QSC`*', 'Global`Q*'.

languageModelTools.name: wolfbook_journalDigest
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Alias of wolfbook_evaluationJournal action="digest": a ~20-line summary of the session (kernel, notebooks touched, last operations, failure/assertion counts).

languageModelTools.name: wolfbook_status
languageModelTools.modelDescription: ONE side-effect-free status surface. scope="all" (default, ~15 lines): connected clients, kernels in this window, recent operations, and the target notebook's state. scope="clients" | "kernels" | "operations" | "notebook" for a single section. Never sends a WSTP packet, never shows an editor, never interrupts running work. To inspect SYMBOLS (which evaluates in the kernel) use wolfbook_inspectSymbols instead.

scope.description: Which section(s) to return. Default all.

notebook.description: Notebook for the notebook section; omit for the session target.

languageModelTools.name: wolfbook_selfTest
languageModelTools.modelDescription: End-to-end self-check of the Wolfbook MCP toolchain: resolves the kernel, evaluates 1+1, creates a temp notebook, verifies the controller association, runs a cell and confirms the symbol landed in the kernel, checks save SHA-256 against disk, checks journal provenance and operation-id resolution, then cleans up. Returns pass/fail per stage. Run after an extension update or when tool behavior seems wrong.

scope.description: quick (default) skips the edit-rerun stage; full runs everything.

keepArtifacts.description: Keep the temp notebook instead of deleting it (for debugging). Default false.

languageModelTools.name: wolfbook_kernelStatus
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Instant, side-effect-free snapshot of Wolfram kernel lifecycle and active operation. Never sends a WSTP packet, waits, or interrupts running work. Use this before probing a possibly busy kernel.

languageModelTools.name: wolfbook_operationStatus
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Read lifecycle, timing, caption, result preview, and bounded progress for a kernel operation ID. This is side-effect-free and never interrupts the kernel.

operation_id.description: Operation ID returned by a Wolfbook execution tool.

after_sequence.description: Return progress entries newer than this sequence number.

wait_seconds.description: Optionally wait this many seconds for completion before returning status.

languageModelTools.name: wolfbook_evaluationJournal
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Return a bounded list of recent kernel operations with captions, targets, timing, state, and result previews. Useful after context compaction or reconnect. action="digest" returns a ~20-line human-readable summary instead (kernel line, notebooks touched, last operations, failure/assertion counts) — the cheapest post-compaction re-orientation call.

action.description: full (default) = JSON journal; digest = summary; export = write a Markdown session report.

state.description: Exact state filter or array of states.

notebook.description: Full notebook path or basename filter.

languageModelTools.name: wolfbook_cancelOperation
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Cancel one specific queued or running Wolfbook operation and always settle its registry record. mode='abort' asks the owning kernel arbiter to abort; mode='discard-result' only discards the operation result and never touches the kernel.

operation_id.description: Operation ID returned by an evaluation tool.

mode.description: abort (default) interrupts matching kernel work; discard-result settles only the registry.

languageModelTools.name: wolfbook_exportSessionReport
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Export a portable Markdown report of retained operations, failures, cancellations, notebook paths, best-effort artifact references, and kernel status. This is the visible alias of evaluationJournal action='export'.

limit.description: Retained for compatibility; reports include every matched retained operation up to 50.

state.description: Exact state filter or array of states.

notebook.description: Full notebook path or basename filter.

languageModelTools.name: wolfbook_saveNotebook
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Save a Wolfbook notebook and verify the exact on-disk bytes by reading them back. Returns canonical path, byte count, mtime, SHA-256, dirty state, and document version.

notebook.description: Notebook filename or absolute path; omit for the active notebook.

languageModelTools.name: wolfbook_getResult
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Read a bounded slice of a completed operation result. Operation IDs are also result handles.

format.description: Return text (default) or pretty-printed JSON when the stored result is valid JSON.

path.description: JSON path into a structured outputForm:'json' result. [] returns a root manifest; non-empty paths return a node manifest plus a bounded slice.

languageModelTools.name: wolfbook_moveCell
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Move or copy a cell within a notebook or between two open notebooks. Within one notebook: reorders atomically. Cross-notebook: reads source cell, inserts into target, then removes from source (or keeps it if copy:true). Use sourceNotebook/targetNotebook to specify notebooks by filename; omit both to use the active notebook as both source and destination. Prefer cellId/afterCellId for stable targeting (numbers shift after edits).

cellId.description: Stable CellId of the source cell. Preferred over cellNumber after structural edits.

cellNumber.description: 1-based number of the cell to move/copy in the source notebook.

toPosition.description: Insert after this 1-based cell number in the target notebook. Use 0 to insert at the very beginning.

afterCellId.description: Stable CellId in the target notebook to insert after. Preferred over toPosition.

sourceNotebook.description: Filename of the source notebook (e.g. 'solver.wb'). Omit to use the active notebook.

targetNotebook.description: Filename of the destination notebook (e.g. 'main.wb'). Omit to move/copy within the same notebook.

copy.description: If true, copy the cell (leave source intact). If false or omitted, move it (delete from source).

expected_cell_id.description: Reject if the resolved source cell ID differs.

languageModelTools.name: wolfbook_restoreDeletedCells
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Lists or restores recently deleted cells from the ai_deleted_cells.md recovery log maintained by wolfbook_deleteCell. Use action="list" to browse the last N deleted cells (default 10) — useful to review what was just removed or to confirm what to restore. Use action="restore" to re-insert the last N deleted cells at a specified position (default: end of notebook). Prefer afterCellId for stable insertion after a specific target cell. The recovery log is never cleared.

action.description: "list" to show recent deleted cells; "restore" to re-insert them into the notebook.

count.description: How many recent deletions to list or restore (default: 10 for list, 1 for restore).

insertPosition.description: Where to insert restored cells: "end" (default) or a 1-based cell number N (inserts after Cell N). Use 0 to insert before Cell 1.

afterCellId.description: Optional stable CellId to restore after. Preferred over insertPosition after structural edits.

languageModelTools.name: wolfbook_kernelControl
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Kernel lifecycle control. restart/checkpoint/restore manage the kernel. abort stops the evaluation currently dispatched to the kernel. To cancel a queued operation by ID, or discard its future result without touching the kernel, use wolfbook_cancelOperation.

action.description: 'restart' to restart the kernel (destructive — clears all state). 'abort' to stop the current evaluation. 'checkpoint' to save all Global` definitions to a .mx file. 'restore' to reload Global` state from a previous checkpoint.

tag.description: Optional label for the checkpoint file (e.g. 'before-refactor'). Only used with action='checkpoint'.

path.description: Path to a specific .mx checkpoint file to restore. Only used with action='restore'. If omitted, restores the most recent checkpoint from this session.

checkpoint_before_restart.description: action='restart' only: auto-checkpoint Global` before restarting. 'if-idle' (default) checkpoints only a healthy idle kernel; 'always' tries even when busy; 'never' skips. Hard 10 s cap; never blocks the restart; the response states truthfully whether a checkpoint was saved.

operation_id.description: For abort: operation expected to own the active kernel evaluation.

reason.description: Human-readable cancellation reason recorded in the journal.

languageModelTools.name: wolfbook_kernelManager
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Lists explicit kernel identities and notebook bindings. With experimental isolation enabled, can create a bounded isolated kernel, bind/unbind a notebook locally, or stop a non-default idle kernel. Bindings never modify the .wb file.

kernel_id.description: Opaque kernel ID returned by action=list.

notebook.description: Notebook path or filename for bind/unbind.

label.description: Optional presentation label for a newly created kernel.

acknowledge_resource_cost.description: Required true for create: acknowledges that another Wolfram process consumes memory and may consume a license seat.

languageModelTools.name: wolfbook_selectKernel
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Select which live Wolfram kernel a notebook uses. Use action=list to discover kernel_id values, action=select to bind a notebook to one of them, action=default to bind it to this VS Code window's default kernel, or action=create to start a new isolated kernel. Multiple notebooks may deliberately share one kernel. Bindings are local VS Code state and never modify the .wb file.

notebook.description: Absolute notebook path. Required for select/default and optional for create.

kernel_id.description: Opaque kernel ID returned by action=list. Required for select.

label.description: Optional label for a newly created kernel.

acknowledge_resource_cost.description: Required true for create because another Wolfram process may consume a license seat.

languageModelTools.name: wolfbook_kernelCrashLog
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Reads the Wolfram kernel debug log (img/<notebookName>/wolfram-kernel-debug.log) and/or macOS crash reports (~/Library/Logs/DiagnosticReports/) to help diagnose kernel crashes and unexpected disconnections. The debug log lives next to btl.log in the notebook's img/ subfolder and is recreated fresh each kernel start. Crash reports contain stack traces from kernel aborts. Use source="debug" for the live debug log, source="crash" for crash reports, source="all" for both.

source.description: "debug" (default) reads the kernel debug log from img/<notebookName>/; "crash" reads macOS DiagnosticReports; "all" reads both.

lines.description: How many tail lines of the debug log to return (default: 150, max: 1000).

filter.description: Optional keyword or regex to filter log lines (case-insensitive). E.g. "ERROR", "ABORT", "crash".

languageModelTools.name: wolfbook_findPackage
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Searches for Wolfram Language packages on the Wolfram Paclet Server (via PacletFindRemote) and on GitHub. Returns names, descriptions, and ready-to-run install commands for each result. For Paclet Server hits the result includes the exact PacletInstall["Name"] command; for GitHub hits it includes the releases URL and explains both the .paclet-URL install path and the URLDownload+ExtractArchive+AppendTo[$Path]+Get workflow for plain source repos. After finding a package, use wolfbook_evaluateExpression with timeoutSeconds>=120 to run the install command — do NOT guess install syntax, always use the commands returned by this tool.

query.description: Search term, e.g. "numerical ODE", "quantum field theory", "cluster algebra". Alphanumeric words and hyphens only.

languageModelTools.name: wolfbook_debugCell
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Controls the Wolfbook step-through debugger. Use action="analyze" to inspect a cell's step structure before debugging. Use action="start" to begin a debug session on a cell (kernel pauses at first step). Use action="status" to check if a session is active and see the last known step info. Use action="stepOver" to execute the current statement and pause at the next one at the same or outer loop level. Use action="stepInto" to enter an inner loop body (pauses at first statement inside). Use action="stepOut" to finish the current loop level and return to the parent. Use action="continue" to run until the next breakpoint. Use action="runToEnd" to run the cell to completion ignoring breakpoints. Use action="stop" to abort the debug session. All step/continue/stop commands require an active session (check with action="status"). Timings are recorded automatically and shown as inline annotations after each session. Use action="addBreakpoint" with a "line" number (1-based) and optional "cellId" or "cellNumber" to set a breakpoint; use action="removeBreakpoint" similarly to remove one; action="clearBreakpoints" removes all (or all for a specific cell if cellId/cellNumber is given); action="listBreakpoints" shows all current breakpoints. Use action="addWatch" with "variableName" to add a variable to the Watch Panel; action="removeWatch" to remove one; action="listWatch" to see the current watch list.

action.description: The operation to perform. Use analyze or start before session; use step/continue/stop while paused; use addBreakpoint/removeBreakpoint/clearBreakpoints/listBreakpoints for breakpoint management; use addWatch/removeWatch/listWatch for the Watch Panel variable list.

cellNumber.description: 1-based cell number for action=analyze, action=start, action=addBreakpoint, action=removeBreakpoint, or action=clearBreakpoints. Omit to use the currently selected cell.

cellId.description: Stable CellId for action=analyze, action=start, action=addBreakpoint, action=removeBreakpoint, or action=clearBreakpoints. Preferred over cellNumber after reordering.

line.description: 1-based line number within the cell. Required for action=addBreakpoint and action=removeBreakpoint.

variableName.description: Wolfram Language variable name for action=addWatch or action=removeWatch.

showInstrumentedCode.description: For action=analyze: if true (default), include the full instrumented code in the result.

languageModelTools.name: wolfbook_fileOps
languageModelTools.modelDescription: File system operations on the local machine. action='read': read the text contents of the file at 'path' (required). action='write': write 'content' string to 'path' (required, creates or overwrites). action='list': list files and subdirectories under directory 'path' (optional, defaults to workspace root); use 'ext' to filter by extension (e.g. '.wl'), 'depth' to control recursion depth (default 4, max 8). All paths should be absolute.

action.description: 'read' to read file contents, 'write' to write file, 'list' to list directory.

path.description: Absolute path to the file or directory. Required for action='read' and action='write'. For action='list', defaults to the first workspace root folder if omitted.

content.description: Text content to write. Required for action='write'.

ext.description: File extension filter for action='list' (e.g. '.wl', '.m'). If omitted, all files are returned.

depth.description: Recursion depth for action='list'. 1 = immediate children only, no subdirectory traversal. Defaults to 4, max 8.

languageModelTools.name: wolfbook_runTerminal
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Runs a shell command and returns stdout/stderr. Use for project-level tasks like builds, tests, scripts, and LaTeX compilation. Keep commands scoped to the workspace.

cwd.description: Optional absolute working directory. Defaults to workspace root.

languageModelTools.name: wolfbook_fairy_dispatch
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Dispatch the Oberon Fairy — a background Wolfram-computation SUB-AGENT running on a cheap local LLM with a heavy verification harness — and return immediately with a runId. USE IT FOR: well-specified, self-contained symbolic/numeric computations that would take many kernel iterations (build+diagonalise a Hamiltonian, solve Bethe-ansatz equations, verify an identity across parameter ranges). It explores in the LIVE kernel, records a reproducible derivation chain, replays it on a fresh kernel, executes your validationChecks, and delivers a verified notebook (clean.wb) plus distilled facts — typical duration 5–30 min, cost ~$0.05. WRITE THE TASK LIKE A CONTRACT: state every parameter (L, boundary conditions, couplings, representation), the exact deliverables, and pass 2–6 validationChecks (Wolfram expressions that must return True or a numeric |value|<1e-8) — the checks are YOUR quality gate over the sub-agent; a vague task wastes the run. CRITICAL: the run RESTARTS the shared Wolfram kernel — do not use wolfbook_evaluateExpression/runCell while it works (your kernel session state is lost), and only one run can be active at a time. Poll wolfbook_fairy_status (~every 60s) for progress and results. Do NOT dispatch tasks needing literature judgment or ambiguous specs — resolve those yourself first.

task.description: Complete, self-contained computation spec: every parameter fixed, deliverables explicit, symbol names suggested (so validationChecks can reference them). 1–2 paragraphs.

validationChecks.description: 2–6 Wolfram Language expressions that independently verify correctness (each must evaluate to True or to a number with |value| < 1e-8), e.g. "Abs[Tr[H]] < 1*^-8", "HermitianMatrixQ[H]". Executed against the delivered chain's kernel; failures block delivery.

languageModelTools.name: wolfbook_fairy_status
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Check the progress/result of a Fairy sub-agent run started with wolfbook_fairy_dispatch. Returns phase (explore/compile/polish/delivered/...), status, probes/turns/cost so far, recent probe notes, the established facts (the distilled results — often all you need), artifact paths (clean.wb = verified deliverable notebook; clean_partial.wb = honest partial report), run metrics, and the build stamp. Omit runId to query the latest run. Poll roughly once a minute while active; when status is 'delivered', read the facts here and open clean.wb (wolfbook_getNotebookContext with the notebook name) if you need the full derivation. 'partial_delivered' means budget ran out or verification failed — the partial report lists what worked, what failed, and how to re-scope a retry.

runId.description: Run id from wolfbook_fairy_dispatch (e.g. "run_2026-07-02T08-31-53-589Z"). Omit for the most recent run.

languageModelTools.name: wolfbook_gold_run
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Start the Oberon GOLD TASK SUITE — the kernel-verified benchmark of the agent pipeline. Each task is dispatched as a real fairy run with an explicit OUTPUT CONTRACT; afterwards the harness restarts a FRESH kernel, replays the delivered clean.wb, and machine-checks the contract symbols with the task's Wolfram verifier (no LLM judging). Use it to (a) record a baseline before changing agent code, and (b) re-measure after a change — compare reports with `node oberon/tests/goldRunner.js compare <base> <cand>`. Pass `tasks` to run a subset (day-to-day usage, e.g. ["GT14","GT01","TS04"]); omitting it runs all 25 tasks (HOURS of wall-clock and real LLM cost — do that deliberately, off-peak). Only one suite/run can be active; each task RESTARTS the shared Wolfram kernel repeatedly. Fire-and-forget: poll wolfbook_gold_status. Reports are written to .oberon/gold/ in the workspace.

tasks.description: Task ids to run, e.g. ["TS01","GT05"]. Omit for the full 25-task suite (expensive; prefer subsets). Ids: TS01–TS10 (research-grade), GT01–GT15 (closed-form).

label.description: Short label stamped into the report filename (e.g. "baseline", "stage1-candidate").

languageModelTools.name: wolfbook_gold_status
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Check progress/results of the Oberon gold task suite started with wolfbook_gold_run. Returns running state plus the latest report: per-task verdicts (verified | false_delivered | partial_verified | partial_failed | sanity_passed | failed — 'false_delivered' means the run CLAIMED success but the fresh-kernel verifier refuted it; investigate those first), verifier detail, per-task cost/LLM calls, and summary metrics (passRate over fully-verifiable tasks, falseDeliveredRate, totalCostUSD, cache hit ratio). Poll every ~2 min while running. The full JSON report (including per-task process-rubric scores) is at the returned reportPath.

languageModelTools.name: wolfbook_paperSearch
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Search AND read academic papers (HEP/math/physics) via INSPIRE-HEP with arXiv fallback. Six actions: (1) 'search' — find papers by title, author, abstract, arXiv ID, INSPIRE texkey, or freeform query; results include title, authors, year, INSPIRE citation count, abstract, ar5iv HTML link, and INSPIRE URL. (2) 'bibtex' — fetch a full BibTeX @article record from INSPIRE. (3) 'bibitem' — fetch a LaTeX \bibitem record (INSPIRE latex-us format). (4) 'references' — list all papers cited BY a paper from INSPIRE (34+ entries typical); add includeContexts:true to also fetch from Semantic Scholar the exact sentences in which each reference is cited. (5) 'citations' — list papers that CITE a given paper, with citation context sentences from Semantic Scholar. (6) 'read' — fetch a paper's FULL TEXT (ar5iv/arXiv HTML) and return section headings, numbered display equations (LaTeX), and the body text most relevant to an optional 'query' focus; requires an arXiv ID; equations are transcriptions — verify before relying on them. Identifier formats accepted: new arXiv IDs ('2103.15840'), old arXiv IDs ('hep-th/0212208'), INSPIRE texkeys ('Gromov:2013pga'), or numeric INSPIRE record IDs. arXiv IDs are resolved via the INSPIRE /api/arxiv/<id> endpoint for reliable lookup. Falls back to arXiv API search for non-HEP papers. Use this tool any time you need to find, cite, or survey academic papers.

author.description: Search by author name (for 'search' action). Use 'Lastname' or 'Lastname, Firstname'.

identifier.description: arXiv ID (e.g. '2103.15840'), INSPIRE texkey (e.g. 'Gromov:2014caa'), or INSPIRE record ID. Used for search (by ID), bibtex, bibitem, references, citations.

query.description: Freeform INSPIRE search query (advanced). Combined with title/author/abstract if both provided.

includeAbstract.description: Include abstracts in search results. Default: true.

includeContexts.description: For 'references' action: also fetch citation contexts from Semantic Scholar showing HOW each reference is used in the text. Default: false.

maxResults.description: Maximum number of results (default: 5 for search, 10 for citations, max 20/50).

maxEquations.description: For action 'read': max display equations to return (default 40, cap 120).

languageModelTools.name: wolfteam_proposePlan
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Call this tool when you have formulated a multi-step calculation plan and need the user to approve it before you begin executing. Pass the plan summary and list of steps. The user will see the plan in a confirmation dialog and click Allow to approve, or Deny to reject. Do NOT execute any steps until this tool returns successfully.

planSummary.description: One-paragraph summary of what the plan will accomplish

steps.description: Ordered list of steps to execute

languageModelTools.name: wolfteam_askDecision
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Call this tool when you reach a conceptual decision point — a choice of gauge, coordinate system, ansatz, expansion strategy, or any fork where the user's physics expertise should guide the direction. Present the question, the available options, and a default. The user can edit the selectedOption parameter before approving. Do NOT guess — always call this tool at genuine decision points.

selectedOption.description: The user's selected option — user can edit this before clicking Allow

context.description: Brief context for why this decision matters

languageModelTools.name: wolfteam_checkpoint
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Call this tool after completing a significant calculation step to show the user the intermediate result and what comes next. The user clicks Allow to continue or Deny to pause and inspect. Use between major steps, not after every trivial evaluation.

result.description: The key result or output (keep concise)

nextStep.description: What will be done next if user approves

languageModelTools.name: wolfteam_askSpecialist
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Call this tool when you need the user's expert input to make a strategic decision — e.g., which paper's conventions to follow, which ansatz to use, which branch of a solution to explore, or which notation to adopt. The question is rendered in Markdown+LaTeX inside the Wolfbook 'Ask Specialist' panel with a blinking background and audio alert so the user notices it. The tool blocks until the user types a reply and submits it. Use this instead of guessing on questions that only the domain expert can answer correctly.

question.description: The question to ask the specialist. May contain Markdown formatting and LaTeX math ($ inline, $$ display). Be specific and concrete.

context.description: Optional background context for the question — e.g., the current approach, relevant equations, or why this decision matters. Rendered above the question.

languageModelTools.name: wolfslide_getContext
languageModelTools.modelDescription:
Returns full deck context: CURRENTLY VISIBLE SLIDE (index + label + block tree), open files, all slide labels with their indices, current theme, style presets, and renderer capabilities. Call this first — it tells you exactly which slide the user is looking at and lists all slides so you can identify the right index before editing.

🚫 NEVER edit .wslide files directly with file/disk tools. All edits must go through wolfslide_* tools — direct file writes bypass the live editor and corrupt the undo stack.

Use 'scope' to anchor the session: wolfslide_getContext(scope:'Fix slide 21 only'). The scope is shown prominently on every subsequent call. Clear with scope:''.

scope.description: Set a task anchor shown at the top of all future getContext calls. Use to stay focused: 'Edit slide 21 only', 'Fix heading styles slides 12-15', etc. Pass empty string to clear.

file.description: Optional: filename or path of the .wslide file to target. Defaults to the active slide editor.

includeCss.description: Set to true to include the full editorCSS in the response. Omitted by default to keep output compact — only needed when inspecting or modifying the CSS.

languageModelTools.name: wolfslide_listSlides
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Returns a summary of all slides (index, label, background, block count, char count, animation steps). By default (verbose:false) shows compact one-line summaries — fast and context-light. Pass verbose:true to include ASCII block trees for ALL slides — WARNING: dumps the entire deck into context, avoid on large decks. For a single slide's block tree, use slideIndex:N (defaults to verbose:true for that one slide) or use wolfslide_getSlide.

slideIndex.description: 1-based slide number. If given, shows only that one slide (verbose defaults true). Use this instead of verbose:true on the full deck.

verbose.description: Include ASCII block trees. Default false (compact). For a single slide use slideIndex:N instead of verbose:true on the full deck.

file.description: Optional: filename or path of the .wslide file to target.

docUri.description: Optional: target a specific open .wslide file.

languageModelTools.name: wolfslide_getSlide
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Returns the ASCII diagram, image summary, and raw JSON for a single slide. Call with NO arguments to see the slide the user is currently looking at — the response includes a '▶ CURRENTLY VIEWING' banner confirming the slide number and label. Use this as the first step when the user says 'this slide' or 'the current slide'. Accepts slideIndex (1-based), slideNumber (alias), or slideId to target a specific slide. Use brief:true to skip the raw JSON — saves context when you only need the ASCII layout.

slideIndex.description: 1-based slide index. Defaults to currently visible slide if omitted.

brief.description: If true, skip the raw JSON block tree. Use when you only need the ASCII layout diagram — much smaller context footprint.

docUri.description: Optional: target a specific open .wslide file.

languageModelTools.name: wolfslide_getSlideHtml
languageModelTools.modelDescription:
Preview a slide. Default (format:'image'): captures a JPEG screenshot of the slide at its FINAL state — all animation fragments visible at once. IMPORTANT: outputPath is REQUIRED for format:'image' — omitting it returns ~100KB base64 inline and exhausts context. Pass outputPath:"/tmp/slide.jpg" (or any absolute path). Use format:'html' to get standalone static HTML without requiring outputPath. Accepts slideIndex (1-based), slideNumber (alias), or slideId. Defaults to the currently visible slide.

⚠ KNOWN CAPTURE LIMITATIONS (format:'image' uses html2canvas, NOT a real browser render): some things can look WRONG in the screenshot even when the live deck is correct — do NOT treat these as bugs/failures: (1) advanced CSS — gradients, backdrop-filter, some box-shadows/text-shadows, and bare-element rules from theme editorCSS (e.g. a custom h2 title bar) — may not be captured; (2) inline <svg> in raw blocks may be blank. For a faithful check of styling, use format:'html', write it to outputPath, and open it in a browser.

slideIndex.description: 1-based slide index. Defaults to currently visible slide if omitted.

format.description: Output format. 'image' (default): JPEG screenshot via html2canvas — shows the final slide state with all elements visible, costs zero extra tokens.
